# Spec — #486: Remote-only (client) install completion

_Milestone 0.13.0, Phase 4, task 7. Written 2026-07-12 against the current branch
(0.13.0-beta.3 baseline + the Phase 1–3 commits already on this branch, notably
#557's shipped `url-policy.ts`/`remote-access-tls.md` and #433's shipped
`DELETE /admin/principals/:id`). Source assessment:
[`../assessments/486.md`](../assessments/486.md) — all line references below were
re-verified against the working tree._

Already merged (verified, no work): `/connections` outside `/admin` in both apps
with capability-guarded `/api/connections/*` (`packages/ui/src/routes/api/connections/`),
the `ConnectionEntry` model with read-time `kind` defaulting
(`packages/ui/src/lib/server/endpoints.ts:29-84`), the `pwa-static` host mode with
public `/api/runtime` (`packages/ui/src/lib/server/features.ts`), the
`@openpalm/client` artifact (IndexedDB store, encrypted secrets, direct transport
with Basic/Bearer auth, CORS-blocked and needs-HTTPS probe disambiguation, PWA
manifest/SW), landing resolvers in both apps routing 0-connection `pwa-static`
sessions to `/connections/new`, guardian `/oc/*` direct ingress
(`GUARDIAN_DIRECT_INGRESS`, port 3830) with the CORS allowlist and the admin API
for minting `direct` principals, and `openpalm app` + the supervised localhost
client server on stable port 3890.

## 0. Decisions (assessment offered options — decided here)

- **D1 — stack-less entry: implement, not document-only.** `openpalm app` gains
  the same not-installed tolerance `openpalm admin` already has
  (`resolveServeState()`), scoped to `openTarget === 'client'`. Rationale: the
  issue's headline is "install as a client only — no local stack"; the delta is
  one branch in `startUIServer` plus two small follow-ons that make the landing
  actually work (D1a, D1b below), all unit-testable with existing harnesses. The
  document-only alternative would leave the CLI hard-failing on the exact
  machine the issue is about.
  - **D1a:** on a machine with no local install, the CLI-written
    `runtime-config.json` must NOT seed the locked "This assistant" connection
    pointing at a dead `http://127.0.0.1:3800` — otherwise the client's landing
    resolver counts 1 stored connection and lands on `/chat` against a dead
    target instead of `/connections/new`. `writeClientRuntimeConfig` (lib)
    accepts `assistantUrl: null` → `connections: []`.
  - **D1b:** `resolveClientOpenTarget` treats `/connections/new` (and
    `/connections`) as client-capable landings and opens them on the CLIENT app
    origin, not the host UI. Today any landing ≠ `/chat` opens the host UI,
    whose `/api/connections` writes are admin-session-gated — a dead end on a
    passwordless stack-less machine. The client app has both routes
    (`packages/client/src/routes/connections/new/+page.ts`).
- **D2 — `openpalm-client-api` kind: wire it (minimally), not descope.** The
  milestone task title names the connection-kind selector, and every storage
  layer already carries the kind — only the two forms and the URL/probe handling
  are missing. Wiring is: a 2-option selector in both add/edit forms
  (`remote-opencode` | `openpalm-client-api`; `local-opencode` stays reserved
  for synthesized entries), `/oc` base-path normalization on save, a kind-aware
  health probe (guardian kind probes the allowlisted `GET /session` instead of
  `GET /` — `GET /oc/` is not an allowlisted route, so the root probe reports a
  healthy guardian as `unreachable HTTP 404`), and guardian-specific copy
  (username hint = principal id; 404 remediation names
  `GUARDIAN_DIRECT_INGRESS`). No transport rewiring beyond an optional
  `probePath` — the `/oc`-prefixed base URL already routes everything else.
- **D3 — remote-credential provisioning: documented manual flow.** A new
  section in `docs/managing-openpalm.md` (enable `GUARDIAN_DIRECT_INGRESS`, add
  the client origin to `GUARDIAN_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, mint a `direct`
  principal via the guardian admin listener with `op_guardian_admin_token`,
  paste id/secret into the client). A host-UI minting affordance is **descoped
  to #511**: the pairing/QR UX (plan §12.3 item 4) owns that surface, and
  building a plain minting button now would be duplicated tracked work
  (assessment risk 1).
- **D4 — end-to-end remote-attach verification: a client-suite e2e test.**
  `packages/client/tests/remote-attach.e2e.test.ts` spawns the real guardian as
  a subprocess (mirroring `packages/guardian/src/proxy-direct.test.ts`) and
  drives it with the real `createTransport` — closing the "each side tested in
  isolation only" gap. It lives in `packages/client/tests/` so it runs under
  the mandated `bun run client:test` gate. The browser-only `'blocked'` CORS
  state cannot be reproduced under Bun (no CORS enforcement outside a browser);
  it stays covered by the existing unit suite
  (`tests/transport-health-cors.test.ts`), and the e2e instead asserts the
  guardian's CORS response headers for an allowlisted Origin — the server half
  of the same contract.

## 1. Scope

Closes these assessment remaining-work items:

1. **Stack-less client entry point** (D1/D1a/D1b): `openpalm app` serves the
   host UI (pwa-static) + localhost client on a machine with no install,
   landing on the client's `/connections/new`.
2. **Wire the `openpalm-client-api` connection kind** (D2) in both connection
   forms + both stores + both health probes.
3. **Remote-credential provisioning path** (D3): documented manual flow in
   `docs/managing-openpalm.md`, cross-linked from `docs/remote-access-tls.md`'s
   audience via `ui-runtime-modes.md`.
4. **End-to-end remote-attach verification** (D4):
   `tests/remote-attach.e2e.test.ts`.
5. **Issue/doc close-out**: `docs/technical/ui-runtime-modes.md` updated to the
   as-built shape (two-artifact split supersedes the issue's "same SvelteKit
   build" text; kind selector wired; stack-less `openpalm app`; pointers to
   #511/#557 for what completes elsewhere). CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` entry.

### Descoped (with justification)

- **Pairing/QR connection setup, hosted-origin (`app.openpalm.dev`) deploy,
  install affordances, `/api/runtime` contract handshake, offline e2e** — all
  explicitly owned by **#511** (plan §12.3 items 2–5; assessment dependency
  note: "#486 should scope itself to the localhost/LAN client story").
- **Host-UI principal-minting affordance** — descoped to #511's pairing UX
  (decision D3); the documented manual flow is the #486 deliverable.
- **HTTPS-for-remote enforcement beyond what shipped** — #557 already shipped
  `validateConnectionUrl()` + the TLS guide;
  `requiresHttpsForRemoteConnections`'s server-side consumer is #511's
  handshake, not this task.
- **mDNS URL auto-fill** — #488 (non-blocking; `/connections` paste flow works
  without it).
- **LAN-preset copy updates** — #563 owns the "#486 framing" copy revision
  (cross-cutting decision in the implementation plan).
- **Browser-lane Playwright e2e for the new form fields** — Playwright browser
  installs are proxy-blocked in the dev container (plan §12.6); the source-pin
  markup idiom (`connections-page-markup.test.ts` house pattern) covers the
  client form, and `svelte-check` covers both forms' types. CI-lane browser
  coverage can be added under #511's e2e item.

## 3. File-level changes

### packages/lib

- **`src/control-plane/client-runtime-config.ts`** — widen
  `writeClientRuntimeConfig(path: string, assistantUrl: string | null, options: WriteClientRuntimeConfigOptions = {}): void`.
  `null` → write `{ connections: [] }` (plus `hostUrl` when passed) instead of
  `buildLockedAssistantRuntimeConfig`. `buildLockedAssistantRuntimeConfig`
  unchanged. Doc comment: a `null` assistant URL is the stack-less client-only
  serve (#486); the client store's `seedFromRuntimeConfig` already deletes a
  previously seeded locked entry absent from the new config, so a later
  `openpalm install` (or uninstall) round-trips cleanly.

### packages/cli

- **`src/lib/ui-server.ts`**
  - `startUIServer` (line 506): replace
    `const state = opts.adminHostUi ? resolveServeState() : ensureValidState();`
    with a tolerance covering the client target:
    `const state = (opts.adminHostUi === true || opts.openTarget === 'client') ? resolveServeState() : ensureValidState();`
    plus a comment citing #486 (client-only machines serve the connection
    manager; the UI's own pwa-static landing handles routing — the CLI
    reimplements no wizard/landing logic). Nothing else in the function
    changes; per the D2-caution comment (lines 579-585) no new early
    return/exit is introduced.
  - `resolveClientOpenTarget` (lines 207-241): introduce
    `const CLIENT_LANDINGS = new Set(['/chat', '/connections', '/connections/new']);`
    Resolve `landingPath` from the probe (default `'/chat'` when the probe is
    null/absent, preserving today's fallback chain including the
    `/api/setup/status` branch). If `landingPath` is NOT in `CLIENT_LANDINGS`
    → `{ url: `${uiUrl}${landingPath}` }` (unchanged). If it IS and the client
    is reachable → open the client at that path:
    `const clientBase = clientUrl.replace(/\/chat$/, '');`
    `{ url: landingPath === '/chat' ? clientUrl : `${clientBase}${landingPath}` }`.
    Otherwise fall back to `{ url: `${uiUrl}${landingPath}`, message: … }`
    (the existing A4 no-exit fallback, message now also emitted for
    non-`/chat` client landings). Update the doc comment.
- **`src/lib/client-server.ts`**
  - `ClientServerDeps` gains
    `hasLocalInstall?: () => boolean` — default
    `() => classifyLocalInstall(resolveStackDir(), resolveOpenPalmHome()) !== 'not_installed'`
    (both already exported from `@openpalm/lib`; add `classifyLocalInstall`,
    `resolveStackDir` to the existing import).
  - `startClientServer`: compute `const installed = hasLocalInstall();` and
    call `writeRuntimeConfig(runtimeConfigPath, installed ? resolveAssistantUrl() : null, { hostUrl: … })`.
    Widen the `writeRuntimeConfig` dep signature's second parameter to
    `string | null` (matches the lib change). `resolveAssistantUrl` is only
    invoked when installed.
- **`src/commands/app.ts`** — update `meta.description` to mention that on a
  machine with no local install it serves the client-only connection manager
  (no logic change; `startUIServer` carries it).

### packages/client (never `@openpalm/lib`; no new dependencies)

- **`src/lib/connections/url-policy.ts`** — add
  `export function normalizeGuardianUrl(rawUrl: string): string`: parse with
  `URL` (unparseable → return input unchanged); strip trailing `/` from the
  pathname; if the pathname does not already end in `/oc`, append `/oc`;
  return `url.toString()` without a trailing slash. Stays a zero-import leaf
  module (purity-safe by construction). Note in the doc comment that
  `packages/ui/src/lib/server/endpoints.ts` carries a deliberate server-side
  twin (`normalizeGuardianOcUrl`) — the client may not import host code and
  vice versa; both are pinned by their own tests (the same accepted
  duplication as `validateConnectionUrl`/`validateEndpointUrl`).
- **`src/lib/transport/index.ts`** — `TransportOptions` gains
  `/** Path probeHealth GETs relative to baseUrl (default '/'). Guardian /oc bases probe an allowlisted route ('/session') because GET /oc/ is not allowlisted and 404s even when healthy (#486). */ probePath?: string;`
  `probeHealth()` (line 530) fetches
  `${base}${options.probePath ?? '/'}`. No other transport change.
- **`src/routes/connections/+page.svelte`**
  - New state `let formKind = $state<'remote-opencode' | 'openpalm-client-api'>('remote-opencode');`
    reset in `openAddForm()`, loaded from `entry.kind` in `openEntryForm()`
    (for `'local-opencode'` locked entries the selector is not rendered —
    kinds are only editable in add/edit modes, and locked entries only open in
    `credentials` mode, which never touches identity fields).
  - Add a `Kind` select in the add/edit branch of the form (beside the URL
    field): options `remote-opencode` → "OpenCode server (direct)" and
    `openpalm-client-api` → "OpenPalm guardian (/oc)". An `onchange` handler
    (NOT `$effect`) sets `formAuthMode = 'basic'` when switching to the
    guardian kind in add mode (guardian principals always use Basic auth).
  - `submitForm()`: after the existing `validateConnectionUrl` check, compute
    `const storedUrl = formKind === 'openpalm-client-api' ? normalizeGuardianUrl(url) : url;`
    and pass `kind: formKind` (add) / `{ label, url: storedUrl, kind: formKind, auth }`
    (edit) — the store's `add`/`update` already accept `kind`.
  - `probeAll()`: build each transport with
    `probePath: entry.kind === 'openpalm-client-api' ? '/session' : '/'`.
  - `healthRemediation()`: additionally return, for a guardian-kind entry in
    `{ state: 'unreachable', detail: 'HTTP 404' }`, copy explaining the
    guardian's direct listener 404s until `GUARDIAN_DIRECT_INGRESS=true` is
    set on the server (deep-link `docs/managing-openpalm.md`'s new section via
    a pinned constant, same idiom as `TLS_GUIDE_URL`). Add
    `export const REMOTE_CLIENT_GUIDE_URL` to `url-policy.ts` pointing at
    `docs/managing-openpalm.md` (pinned by test 21's regex + the existing
    guide-file-exists pattern in `connections-url-policy.test.ts`).
  - Basic-auth username hint: when `formKind === 'openpalm-client-api'`, the
    `<small>` reads that the username is the **guardian principal id** (not
    the `openpalm` default).
- **`src/lib/connections/index.ts`, `src/lib/boot.ts`, chat page** — no
  changes (kind already typed and persisted; transport auth unchanged).

- **`src/lib/server/endpoints.ts`**
  - `export const USER_ADDABLE_CONNECTION_KINDS = ['remote-opencode', 'openpalm-client-api'] as const;`
  - Add `export function normalizeGuardianOcUrl(url: string): string` (same
    rule as the client twin; operates on an already-`normalizeEndpointUrl`-ed
    string, so only the `/oc` suffix logic is needed).
  - `ConnectionInput` (line 367) gains `kind?: ConnectionKind`;
    `addConnection` validates `input.kind` against
    `USER_ADDABLE_CONNECTION_KINDS` (throw `Error('Invalid connection kind')`
    otherwise), applies `normalizeGuardianOcUrl` when the kind is
    `openpalm-client-api`, and spreads `...(input.kind ? { kind: input.kind } : {})`
    into the entry (no `kind` key when unset — legacy on-disk shape
    preserved, test 30).
  - `ConnectionPatch` (line 389) gains `kind?: ConnectionKind`;
    `updateConnection` validates and applies it, and re-normalizes `next.url`
    with `normalizeGuardianOcUrl` when the EFFECTIVE kind (patched or
    existing) is `openpalm-client-api` and a URL is part of the patch.
    Switching a guardian entry back to `remote-opencode` does not attempt to
    strip `/oc` (the stored URL is authoritative; documented in the doc
    comment).
  - `probeEndpoint` (line 444): probe
    `endpoint.kind === 'openpalm-client-api' ? `${endpoint.url}/session` : endpoint.url`.
- **`src/routes/api/connections/+server.ts`** — POST parses
  `body.kind`: absent → omitted; a string in
  `USER_ADDABLE_CONNECTION_KINDS` → passed to `addConnection`; anything else →
  `400 invalid_connection` (`'kind must be remote-opencode or openpalm-client-api'`).
- **`src/routes/api/connections/[id]/+server.ts`** — PATCH: same optional
  parse into `patch.kind`.
- **`src/routes/connections/+page.svelte`** — mirror the client form: a
  `formKind` state + the same 2-option `Kind` select in add/edit; include
  `kind` in the POST/PATCH payloads; render the kind on each connection card
  (small text/badge, `guardian` for `openpalm-client-api`) so users can tell
  entries apart. `publishConnection` already returns `kind` — no API-client
  change beyond the payload fields.

### packages/guardian

- **No changes.** Direct principals, `DELETE /admin/principals/:id`, direct
  ingress, and the CORS allowlist are all shipped; the e2e consumes them as-is.

### Docs

- **`docs/managing-openpalm.md`** — new section under Common Tasks:
  **"Connect a remote client (another computer or phone)"**:
  1. `GUARDIAN_DIRECT_INGRESS=true` in `knowledge/env/stack.env` (+ what it
     exposes: the guardian direct listener on
     `${OP_BIND_ADDRESS:-127.0.0.1}:${OP_GUARDIAN_PORT:-3830}`; loopback
     default unchanged — reaching it from another machine needs either the
     TLS front from `docs/remote-access-tls.md` (recommended, required for
     phones) or an explicit non-loopback `OP_BIND_ADDRESS` on a trusted LAN).
  2. Add the **client app's origin** to `GUARDIAN_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`
     (exact origin, no wildcard; note the shipped default already covers the
     localhost client origins).
  3. Mint a `direct` principal on the loopback-only admin listener:
     `curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3831/admin/principals -H "authorization: Bearer $(cat ~/.openpalm/knowledge/secrets/op_guardian_admin_token)" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"id":"my-phone","kind":"direct","token":"<openssl rand -hex 24>","label":"My phone"}'`
     (+ rotate/disable/delete one-liners referencing the same endpoints).
  4. In the client's `/connections`: kind **OpenPalm guardian (/oc)**, URL =
     the guardian's base URL (`/oc` is appended automatically), auth Basic
     with **username = the principal id** and password = the token.
  5. `docker compose … up -d guardian` to apply env changes; troubleshooting
     table: 404 → ingress off; `blocked (CORS)` → origin missing from the
     allowlist; `auth failed` → id/token mismatch.
  Security framing: fail-closed defaults untouched; content validation still
  screens direct-tier prompts; never put the token in `stack.env` (it lives
  only in the guardian's state DB and the client's encrypted store).
- **`docs/technical/ui-runtime-modes.md`** — update: `openpalm app` serves
  stack-less (pwa-static + client, landing `/connections/new`); the
  `openpalm-client-api` kind is wired in both forms (guardian `/oc`
  normalization + `/session` probe); Security Boundaries gains a pointer to
  the provisioning section; a short "as-built vs. issue text" close-out note
  for #486 (two-artifact split supersedes "same SvelteKit build,
  capability-hidden"); "Not Yet Shipped" keeps hosted install + pairing under
  #511 (unchanged).
- **`CHANGELOG.md`** — `[Unreleased]` → `### Added`: remote-only (client)
  install completion (#486): stack-less `openpalm app`, guardian connection
  kind in both connection forms, documented remote-client provisioning flow,

## 4. Acceptance mapping

Issue acceptance criteria (as-built interpretation per the ratified
two-artifact split; the issue's own "resolved" bullets):

| Criterion | Proof |
|---|---|
| Client-only install: no local stack, UI is the only process; no Docker, no `/api/host/*` | Tests 1–3 (`openpalm app` serves on not-installed OP_HOME; no docker spawn; bare serve unchanged) + existing `tests/purity.test.ts` (client artifact has no host APIs) |
| Landing at `/connections/new` after a "set up later"/no-connection start | Tests 4–8 (client-capable landing opens the CLIENT `/connections/new`; empty runtime config on stack-less machines so the client resolver counts 0 connections) + existing `resolve-landing` suites (shipped) |
| `/connections` add/switch/manage reachable without host admin | Shipped (characterization pinned in `server.vitest.ts`); unchanged by this task |
| `ConnectionEntry.kind` incl. `openpalm-client-api` is a real, selectable kind | Tests 17–22 (client form), 29–37 (host store + API), 10–13 (URL rule) |
| Remote assistant attach goes through Guardian `/oc/*` with Basic auth aligned with #435 | Tests 23–28 (`remote-attach.e2e.test.ts`: real guardian + real client transport, direct principal, id-as-username Basic auth) |
| Remote endpoint authentication is provisionable by a user | D3 doc section in `docs/managing-openpalm.md` (artifact) + test 27 pinning the CORS/ingress knob pair the doc teaches + tests 21–22 (client UI names the knobs/username rule) |
| Connection status surfaced in `/connections` (incl. guardian-specific failure modes) | Tests 14–16, 20–21, 28 (kind-aware probe; 404-ingress remediation; existing CORS/insecure badges unchanged) |
| `pwa-static` mode starts no containers / issue close-out reflects as-built shape | Test 2 + `ui-runtime-modes.md` update (artifact) |
| PWA install path | Shipped (manifest/SW, `tests/pwa-config.test.ts`); remaining install-path items tracked in #511 (descoped, recorded in §1) |

## 5. Verification gates (implementer must run green, in order)

1. `bun install` (repo root only — single-lockfile rule; expected no-op)
2. `bun run lint`
3. `bun run check`
4. `bun run cli:test`
5. `bun run client:build && bun run client:test` (the build must precede the
   test run — the purity gate greps the built bundle, and the e2e needs only
   sources; `remote-attach.e2e.test.ts` spawns the guardian from
   `packages/guardian/` sources)
6. `bun run ui:check`

Additionally (touched-package suites, per the milestone execution model):
`bun run lib:test`, `bun run ui:test:unit`, and a final `bun run test`
aggregate compared against the pre-change baseline (known sandbox flakes in
lib's root-uid ownership tests are baseline, not regressions).

## 6. Risks and how the design avoids them

- **Scope creep into #511** (assessment risk 1): pairing/QR, hosted origin,
  minting UI, and install affordances are explicitly descoped (§1) with the
  provisioning need met by docs only (D3).
- **Loosening `ensureValidState()` destabilizes the hardened D1/D2/A4
  supervisor logic** (risk 2): the change is a single ternary arm reusing the
  ALREADY-SHIPPED `resolveServeState()` path `openpalm admin` exercises daily;
  no supervisor/probe/teardown code moves. Test 3 pins that bare serve still
  requires an install; tests 1–2 pin the new arm; `resolveClientOpenTarget`
  changes stay inside the existing never-exit contract (tests 4–6) and the
  D2-caution comment region gains no early returns.
- **Implementing the issue text literally vs. the two-artifact split**
  (risk 3): the spec builds only on the as-built shape (client artifact +
  pwa-static host mode) and updates `ui-runtime-modes.md` to record the
  close-out reading (§3 Docs).
- **Weakening the loopback/fail-closed posture via the convenience flow**
  (risk 4): zero default changes — `GUARDIAN_DIRECT_INGRESS` stays `false`,
  binds stay loopback, the doc flow is explicit operator opt-in and reiterates
  the I3 rule; the client server stays loopback-pinned
  (`client-server.ts` HOST pin untouched); no secret enters `stack.env` or
  logs; the minted token flows only via the admin listener (loopback,
  bearer-gated) and the client's encrypted store.
- **Two-knob "blocked (CORS)" dead end** (risk 5): the doc names both knobs in
  one flow; the client already renders CORS remediation naming both, and this
  task adds the missing third failure mode (404 → ingress off, tests 21/28).
- **Proxy-blocked browser lanes** (risk 6): every new test runs under
  bun/vitest-node; the e2e uses subprocess HTTP on loopback, not a browser.
  The one genuinely browser-only behavior (CORS `'blocked'` classification)
  keeps its existing mocked unit coverage; the server half is asserted in
  test 27.
- **Client purity gate**: no new client dependencies; `url-policy.ts` stays a
  zero-import leaf; the e2e's cross-package imports (`oc-doc-fixture.ts`,
  spawning guardian sources) are test-only and never enter the built bundle
  (the purity test greps `build/`). The deliberate `/oc`-normalizer twin in
  `packages/ui` is documented at both sites (established
  `validateConnectionUrl` precedent, since `@openpalm/client` may not import
  host code).
- **e2e flakiness/cost**: mirrors the proven `proxy-direct.test.ts` harness
  (port allocation, readiness polls, drift-gate wait, generous timeouts);
  two guardian spawns total, torn down in `afterAll`.

## 7. Out of scope (explicit)

- Pairing/QR + one-time-code UX, hosted-origin CI deploy, `/api/runtime`
  contract-version handshake, install affordances, `clientDisplayMode`
  detection work, offline Playwright e2e — **#511**.
- Any server-side enforcement consuming `requiresHttpsForRemoteConnections`;
  further TLS tooling — **#557 shipped its half; the rest is #511's handshake**.
- mDNS discovery/URL auto-fill — **#488**.
- Network-access presets, `OPENCODE_AUTH` plumbing, LAN-copy revisions — **#563**.
- Guardian schema/auth changes (`cert_fingerprint`, Bearer surface changes) —
  **#433/#435** (both closed on this branch; the e2e consumes their shipped
  surface only).
- Host-UI principal-minting affordance (deferred to #511 pairing, decision D3).
- Renaming `endpoints.json`, data migrations, or retiring the legacy
  endpoint-language aliases in `endpoints.ts`.
- Electron harness changes (its client runtime-config writer already has a
  host process by definition; `HARNESS_CONTRACT_VERSION` untouched).
- Stripping `/oc` when a connection's kind is switched away from
  `openpalm-client-api` (stored URL stays authoritative).
